candidate.name: SINGLE_CANONICAL_EFFECT_TRANSACTION_WITH_SEMANTIC_REQUEST_BINDING
candidate.core_rule: In canonical-effect mode, F2 does not own a second real-effect executor call. F2 prepares call correlation plus an immutable semantic request identity; the admitted canonical EffectGate owns the one execution transaction; F2 consumes canonical result evidence only for correlation and later completion verification.
required_pre_entry_binding: typed effect request under the admitted canonical EffectRequest ABI
deterministic effect_request_sha256 over exact policy-and-execution semantics
binding_id, invocation_id, tool_use_id, delegation_id and child_identity_sha256
required_result_binding: same effect_request_sha256 echoed or independently recomputable from the request consumed by EffectGate
same F2 call correlation identity or deterministic adapter binding
terminal or unknown status classified only from canonical execution/journal evidence
candidate.dispatch_law: Exactly one component owns the real action invocation; under this candidate that owner is the admitted canonical EffectGate transaction, not a second F2 executor call.
candidate.recovery_law: After possible canonical dispatch, loss of control remains UNKNOWN until canonical EffectJournal recovery/query resolves it; F2 never replays the action automatically.

why_this_candidate_is_needed: Current F2 call/evidence structures bind correlation identity but not immutable action/target/capability/argv semantics.
Canonical EffectGate.execute already owns policy checks, journal PENDING creation, action execution and terminal journal transition.
Using EffectGate.execute as an authorize callback followed by the existing F2 executor risks double dispatch.
Using EffectJournal.begin directly avoids double dispatch but bypasses EffectGate policy/replay/lease checks.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Keep authorize-then-F2-executor and adapt EffectGate.execute into authorize.
counterhypotheses.reason: EffectGate.execute already owns effect execution and journal finalization.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Use EffectJournal.begin as authorization and keep F2 executor.
counterhypotheses.reason: Journal reservation does not perform full EffectGate policy/replay/lease checks.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Existing correlation IDs already imply semantic effect request identity.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: Produce exact current source proving deterministic immutable resolution from a bound F2 identifier to the complete canonical EffectRequest and that canonical execution plus F2 completion correlation verify the same request digest.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: EntityOS should add a prepare/dispatch/finalize split API.
counterhypotheses.reason: Only valid if canonical EntityOS owns and admits the semantic API change including lease custody and recovery; F2 must not invent it locally.

matrix: same call + same effect_request_sha256 -> canonical stub/noop transaction invokes action at most once and returns correlatable canonical receipt
mutated action/target/capability/argv with same call identity -> reject before action
same semantic request with mutated call identity -> reject before action
authority repository/path/blob/schema/API mismatch -> zero action invocation
exception after canonical execution boundary -> F2 UNKNOWN plus canonical journal reconciliation; zero automatic replay
restart with residual PENDING -> canonical recovery classification; zero automatic replay
verified canonical result -> execution correlation allowed but completion still requires separate WP105 verification
deterministic_no_real_effect_discriminat.acceptance: One and only one canonical action invocation; exact semantic request identity is preserved across policy evaluation, canonical journal/effect identity and F2 correlation; every pre-dispatch mismatch fails closed; post-dispatch ambiguity never becomes a negative world fact or replay authorization.

implementation_note_for_active_mutation_: Prefer a F2 correlation wrapper around one canonical EffectGate-owned transaction instead of wiring EffectGate.execute into the current authorize callback followed by a second executor. Keep effect_executor_interlock as external-authorizer/test compatibility unless the active WP105 authority deliberately changes its role.
next_exact_action_for_active_mutation_au: Implement or falsify this candidate only inside the existing WP105 mutation lane by binding one deterministic semantic effect_request_sha256 before authority entry and proving a one-call canonical no-real-effect/noop transaction with exact mismatch and UNKNOWN/no-replay tests.
